hostOS is ubuntu of the Debian family, read from every worker's os-release. It is what ubuntuHost is decided by, and the one distribution that decides it is Ubuntu, whose NVMe-oF modules are in a package the base install does not carry
enableDriveFormat is set, so every drive listed here is formatted before a storage node takes it: a drive that carries anything is not usable otherwise. This is the line to remove if any of them should be left alone.
vcpuCount is 16, the cores of the memory node chosen on worker-01, which is the smallest of the fleet: the control plane assumes this uniform across a cluster's nodes
maxSubsystemCount is 30, which is the middle of the range this API accepts and not a reading: how many subsystems a node should serve follows from the workload rather than from the hardware
minHugePagesSize is 16G, the huge pages free on the memory node chosen on worker-01, which is the smallest of the fleet
enableJournalDevice is set because spec.discover.forceJournalDevice asked for it: the smallest disk of every node carries the journal instead of data, the smallest named being 2T (/dev/sdb) on worker-01. This is the line to remove to carve the journal from a partition instead
stripe is 2+1 as a single-node cluster (clusterMode Single): each chunk of a stripe lands on its own device of the one worker, which hands over 4 for data, so the cluster survives 1 device failure but not the loss of the worker; data migration after a device failure runs in relaxed placement on the same node. The devices would also carry 1+1, 1+2, 2+2, which trade capacity for a second tolerated device failure or the other way about. A cluster meant to grow to more workers is not created as Single and states the stripe of the fleet it will have. A cluster's stripe cannot be changed afterward
